To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a Ca2+ extrusion mechanism in smooth muscle cells can be activated by a protein kinase C activator, and that this activation does not lead to changes in intracellular Ca2+-mobilizing hormone-induced Ca2+ transi
the Na+/ Ca2+ antiporter, an electrogenic exchanger, is present in a smooth muscle cell line, and that the antiporter can be activated by phorbol myrisate acetate, an activator of protein kinases.
the Na+/H+ and Na+/Ca2+-exchanger systems are activated by protein kinase C in aorta-derived cells and that the Na+/K+ pump is not.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulation of the Na+/H+ and Na+/Ca2 + exchangers by protein kinase C and the role of protein kinase C in the regulation of the cytoplasmic Na+ and Ca2+ concentrations in vascular smooth muscle cells.
the characterization of a Na+/Ca2+-exchange system in vascular smooth muscle and with its regulation by protein kinase C.
the characterization of a Na+/Ca2+-antiporter in smooth muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Na+/ Ca2+ antiporter of the smooth muscle cells is electrogenic and is activated by phorbol myrisrate acetate.
the Na+/H+ exchanger in the smooth muscle cell is a target for the action of the Ca2+/phospho-lipid-dependent protein kinase.
the Na+/H+ exchanger in vascular smooth muscle is activated by a variety of agents that increase intracellular Ca2+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Na+/ Ca2+ antiporter plays an important role in Ca2+ homeostasis in smooth muscle cells and is regulated by the Ca2+/phospho-lipid-dependent enzyme.

the Na+/Cai antiporter in smooth cells is electrogenic, is activated by phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), is not involved in Ca2+ translocation in response to vasopressin and is not involved in regulation of the intracellular Ca2+.
the Na+/H+ and the Na+/Ca+ antiporters in A7r5 aortic smooth muscle cell line are activated by phorbol-esters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+/ Ca2+ antiporter can be activated by protein kinase C and that this activation may play an important role in the control of intracellular Na+ homeostasis.
the Na+/H+ antiporter is a target for PKC in smooth muscle cells.
